text:
marta: Quick thread — saved-views in Console (per-route / per-model) are showing routing presets and quota hints that are misleading after a canary flip. Folks are reporting they think the saved view pins a model but it actually just pinned a policy id. Can we decide whether the Console should show computed/effective routing or only the policy?

ken: Can you repro with a concrete flow? screenshot or steps?

marta: Steps: 1) open route /payments -> models tab, 2) select preset 'low-latency', 3) save view -> share. Recipient loads it and sees header: "Active model: model-gamma" but traffic is routed to model-gamma-quant; the header never indicates fallback to model-epsilon. Users assume saved view forces model-gamma. :confused:

sam: Sounds like our view API currently returns the saved preset id and the routing_policy id but not the computed variant. We only compute effective routing at inference time (router service). We can either a) snapshot the effective model at save time, b) compute on load and show a preview, or c) show only policy id and add explanatory microcopy.

alex: My preference is (b) — compute on load. That avoids stale snapshots when a model variant is swapped or retired. But we should surface both: "policy: latency-7" and "preview: model-gamma-quant (fallback: model-epsilon)" with a small as-of timestamp. Also emit telemetry when preview differs from policy.

marta: Agree with showing both. UX suggestion: keep saved view semantics "policy first" but show a compact preview row under the title: "Preview routing (at load): ..." with a tooltip: "This is the computed route for your current tenancy/traffic. It may change if policies or capacity change." :eyes:

ken: Operational question: if we compute on load, how expensive is the compute? Router does a small policy resolution; should be cheap but we must ensure not to blow up calls for large lists of saved views in dashboards. Perhaps cache previews for ~60s per-tenant.

sam: Example API shape proposal (minimal):

GET /api/v1/views/123?expand=effective_routing
Response (preview):
```
{
  "view_id": "123",
  "filters": {"route": "payments", "model_tag": "realtime"},
  "policy_id": "latency-7",
  "routing_preview": "model-gamma-quant -> fallback model-epsilon",
  "routing_preview_as_of": "2025-06-20T04:12:03Z",
  "quota_hint": "preview: 180 req/min"
}
```

sam: If expand is omitted, we return the policy_id only. This lets console list endpoints avoid compute by default.

alex: Telemetry hooks we should add: view.load.preview.routing (fields: view_id, policy_id, preview_model, preview_diff_bool, tenant_id). Also view.save.snapshots.include_policy (if we ever add snapshot option).

devex: Small copy + rollout UX note: for initial rollout, surface preview behind a feature flag and add a "why does this differ?" help link that explains canary/burst capacity and model variants. For sharing: when user clicks "share snapshot" we should offer two modes: "share policy" (default) and "share snapshot (pin effective model)" — explicit opt-in.

marta: That solves most concerns. Can we also show quota-peek in the header? Something like "expected throughput: 180 rps (preview) — estimate only". People confuse quota hints for guarantees.

ken: Agree. Implementation plan: backend: router service exposes /resolve_policy?policy_id=..&tenant=.. -> returns preview + cost estimate. Console: call resolve_policy for single-view load behind expand flag. Cache TTL 60s. Devex: UX strings. Telemetry: alex.

sam: I'll draft the API PR: add expand param and wire to router.resolve endpoint, include unit tests for caching behavior. ETA: EOD today for a draft.

marta: Thanks — @sam please @ken+@alex on the PR so we can iterate quickly. :rocket:

infra-bot: deploybot: preview-api/v2 scheduled to canary at 2025-06-20T04:00Z (build 8421) :truck: 

ken: +1 on timeline. If we hit edgecases (list loads w/ many saved views) we can gate behind FF.

sam: on it. will post PR link when ready.

marta: Great — follow-up meeting if needed after PR review. Thanks all! :+1:
